info.name: ENVISION Runtime API
info.description:
ENVISION Runtime API collection aligned with Controllers/API.cs.

All requests authenticate via HTTP Basic auth (Authorization header).
Set the collection variables 'base_url', 'username' and 'password' before use.

Variable names are free-form since schema v68. Use the full canonical name as returned by GetVariableList or GetVariableDictionary (e.g. 'PLC.Temperature', 'IP1_Speed', or 'Counter').
Historic alarm/event endpoints use a simplified request body: startDatetime, endDatetime and optional search. They always return at most 10000 rows ordered by OnTime DESC.
Admin-only runtime endpoints are included for parameter reads and updates.

request.description:
Subscribe to a list of variables and get their current values.
Body: JSON array of full canonical variable names as returned by GetVariableList or GetVariableDictionary.
Returns a JSON array where each item contains: Name, Value, TimeStamp, Units and Status.

Read a single variable by its full canonical name.
Use the exact name returned by GetVariableList or GetVariableDictionary.
Returns a response object with Variable, Value, TimeStamp, Status and Units.

Retrieve historic trend data for a variable.
Since schema v68 variable names are full canonical names (free-form), so the historian is queried by the variable name alone; there is no separate device field.
Datetime format: ISO 8601 round-trip (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ).
Returns a JSON array where each item contains: Value and TimeStamp.

Returns the current active/returned-unacknowledged alarm list, aligned with AlarmViewer.
Each item includes state flags, timestamps and both configured and resolved alarm messages.
No request body is required.

Returns historic alarms between two dates.
Request body fields: startDatetime, endDatetime and optional search.
The API always applies ORDER BY OnTime DESC with a maximum of 10000 rows.
Datetime format: ISO 8601 round-trip (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ).

Returns historic events between two dates.
Request body fields: startDatetime, endDatetime and optional search.
The API always applies ORDER BY OnTime DESC with a maximum of 10000 rows.
Datetime format: ISO 8601 round-trip (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ).

Records an electronic signature and returns a single-use token, for actions that require a signature in Part 11 compliance mode.
The signature must belong to the authenticated caller: Basic auth callers sign for their own user name.
Repeat the protected request with the returned token in the X-Signature-Token header. The token is bound to the action key and user and expires after 2 minutes.
Action keys currently used by the runtime alarm endpoints: Alarm.Ack.
MCP clients run the same flow with the SignAction tool and pass the token as the signatureToken argument of the protected tool.

Acknowledges one or more active alarms, the same action as the Acknowledge button on the Alarm Viewer.
AlarmIds are the Id values returned by Get Active Alarms. Comment is optional.
Requires the Alarm Acknowledge right on one of the calling user's user groups.
Acknowledging more than one alarm in a single call also requires the Alarm Acknowledge All right.
When compliance mode requires an electronic signature for Alarm.Ack, the call answers with signatureRequired.
Run Sign Action (Signature Verify) first and repeat this request with the returned token in the X-Signature-Token header.

Acknowledges one historic alarm.
AlarmId is the Id value returned by Get Historic Alarms. Comment is optional.
Requires the Alarm Acknowledge right on one of the calling user's user groups.
When compliance mode requires an electronic signature for Alarm.Ack, the call answers with signatureRequired.
Run Sign Action (Signature Verify) first and repeat this request with the returned token in the X-Signature-Token header.

Removes one or more active alarms from the active alarm list without acknowledging them, the same action as Remove on the Alarm Viewer.
AlarmIds are the Id values returned by Get Active Alarms.
Requires the Alarm Remove Active right on one of the calling user's user groups.
Removing more than one alarm in a single call also requires the Alarm Remove All Active right.
Each removal is recorded in the audit trail. The historic alarm record is kept.

Write a value to a variable by its full canonical name.
Use the exact name returned by GetVariableList or GetVariableDictionary.
The authenticated user must have write rights for the target variable.
Returns 'OK' on success.

Restart one running device by name.
The driver connection is closed, the device configuration is re-read from Configuration.db and a new driver thread is started, so a restart also applies any pending configuration changes for that device.
The restart is queued and takes a few seconds to complete; follow the '<DeviceName>.ChannelState' variable for progress.
Restarting an MQTT device name restarts its parent MQTT client and every device that belongs to it.
Requires the caller's user group to carry DeviceConnectionControlRight; members of the Administrators group always pass. A caller without the right is refused with 'User does not have the rights to restart devices.' and the refusal is recorded in the audit trail as DeviceRestartDenied.
Rejected on a standby server and for an unknown device name.
Signature-gated under action key 'Device.Restart' when compliance mode is enabled: sign with POST API/Signature/Verify and retry with the X-Signature-Token header.
Returns 'OK' on success.

Execute a read-only SQL query against a configured database.
Supported databases depend on the ENVISION installation.

Executes the Python script whose EndPoint field matches the last URL segment (dynamic endpoint feature).
Set the collection variable 'script_endpoint' to the script's EndPoint value.
The script must be enabled and must not be a module.
Access follows the script's User Groups; when the script has no user groups, only Administrators may execute it.
The entire request body is passed to the script and is readable inside the script with GetParam('body').
Returns the script's printed output.
